title: Pedro Henrique da Costa Avelar
text:
Biography
Pedro is interested in developing causal representation learning and neuro-symbolic methods to improve the generalisability, fairness, and interpretability of medical AI. His past experience includes using Graph Neural Networks and Transformers for symbolic problems and computer vision, multi-omics integration and prior-knowledge-based omics analysis, and analysing biases in Machine Translation.

title: Matthew Sperrin
text:
Biography
Matt Sperrin is Professor of Biostatistics and Health Data Science at University of Manchester. Matt is a statistician by background, with research interests at the intersection of prediction modelling and causal inference. He is especially interested in how causal inference can be used to allow prediction under intervention (i.e., what would be the risk IF…), and how causal principles can help to ensure prediction models are generalisable and fair. He programme directs the MSc Health Data Science, and co-leads CHAI (the causality in healthcare AI hub).

title: Glen Martin
text:
Biography
Glen is a Senior Lecturer in Health Data Science in the Division of Informatics, Imaging and Data Science at the University of Manchester. His research focuses on developing methodology for clinical risk prediction models, with expertise in multivariate modelling, missing data, and model translation. He holds a PhD in Health Data Science and is a Chartered Statistics. He is Programme Director for the MSc Health Informatics programme, jointly delivered with UCL, and is a Fellow of the Higher Education Academy.

title: Siân Bladon
text:
Biography
Sian is an experienced health data scientist currently working as a Lecturer in Health Data Sciences within the Division of Informatics, Imaging and Data Science at the University of Manchester. Sian previously worked as a PDRA on the CONNECT project, developing a clinical prediction model to predict the risk of relapse in people with psychosis using data collected through wearable devices and smartphones. Her current research interests focus on addressing the challenges of incorporating high-frequency data (e.g. from wearable devices) into clinical prediction models. Sian teaches primarily on the MSc Health Data Science and Health Informatics programmes, contributing to teaching on statistics, data visualisation, data linkage and digital transformation.
